paper_title: AgentOccam: A Simple Yet Strong Baseline for LLM-Based Web Agents
summary:
AgentOccam: A Simple Yet Strong Baseline for LLM-Based Web Agents - Ke Yang, Yao Liu, Sapana Chaudhary, Rasool Fakoor, Pratik Chaudhari, George Karypis, Huzefa Rangwala, 2025

AgentOccam targets the mismatch between how web environments expose state and actions and how general-purpose LLMs are trained to process text and generate language. Instead of adding planners, search procedures, evaluators, memory modules, or task-specific prompt templates, it asks whether a strong web agent can be built by optimizing only the observation mapping and action mapping around a base LLM policy. The framework has three concrete components. First, it compresses the action space by removing non-essential low-level browser operations and packaging interaction into a smaller set of higher-utility commands, reducing embodiment burden on the model. Second, it rewrites the observation space by pruning redundant and irrelevant DOM content and restructuring page content blocks into a more succinct but still informative textual representation. Third, it adds two planning actions, branch and prune, which let the same LLM generate and edit a planning tree inline with normal navigation, while also using the active subplan to selectively replay only relevant history. The implementation is rule-based over markup pages and does not use in-context examples, auxiliary roles, online search, or search-time sampling. On WebArena’s 812 tasks across shopping, shopping admin, GitLab, map, Reddit, and multisite settings, AgentOccam reaches 43.1% success rate with GPT-4-Turbo, versus 33.3% for a SteP replication, 37.2% for WebPilot, and 35.5% for AWM, yielding +9.8 absolute points over the prior SOTA and +5.9 over concurrent work. Relative to a plain WebArena-style GPT-4-Turbo agent at 16.5%, the gain is +26.6 points, or +161%. It also improves per-site performance to 40.6% on shopping, 45.6% on shopping admin, 37.8% on GitLab, 46.8% on map, 61.3% on Reddit, and 14.6% on multisite. ([assets.amazon.science](https://assets.amazon.science/e8/9b/35bdbcb9448da1083ec5710b7c75/agentoccam-a-simple-yet-strong-baseline-for-llm-based-web-agents.pdf))

The ablation study shows that the gains come from representation alignment rather than hidden architectural complexity. Removing non-essential actions raises WebArena-dev success from 14.2% to 25.8% with GPT-4-Turbo; disabling arbitrary scrolling increases it to 30.0%; observation simplification raises it to 34.7%; selective history replay reaches 36.8%; and the full system with planning actions reaches 44.2%. The same trend transfers to Gemini-1.5-Flash, where performance rises from 11.6% for the vanilla agent to 33.7% for full AgentOccam, indicating the method is not specific to the GPT family. The planning-tree mechanism is operational rather than decorative: branch creates subplans, prune restores earlier task states, and the active subplan defines the scope of navigation and the subset of prior observations replayed into context, which reduces irrelevant history while preserving long-horizon task structure. On real websites, the method generalizes to a 129-task deterministic-answer subset of WebVoyager spanning 13 sites, where it scores 54.3% versus 51.9% for a replicated Agent-E baseline, with notable wins on Booking, Cambridge Dictionary, ESPN, Google Maps, Google Search, and Hugging Face. Token and action statistics further support the mechanism: action-space reduction cuts average observation tokens per step from 2210.2 to 1652.0 on WebArena, while the final system uses planning actions to recover performance and lower context relative to history-heavy variants. The paper’s central empirical claim is therefore that careful alignment of textual observations and executable actions is an orthogonal, high-leverage design axis for web agents, and can outperform substantially more elaborate multi-module or search-based systems in zero-shot settings. ([assets.amazon.science](https://assets.amazon.science/e8/9b/35bdbcb9448da1083ec5710b7c75/agentoccam-a-simple-yet-strong-baseline-for-llm-based-web-agents.pdf))
